nodes.description: Autoimmune NMDA receptor dysfunction provides one etiological route to catatonia in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. The downstream circuit sequence generating catatonic signs remains uncertain. Published case reports document both hypokinetic and excited signs, sometimes in the same patient. This subgroup does not establish microglial activation or a general NMDA signaling abnormality in every form of catatonia.

nodes.description: Reduced cortical GABA-A-mediated inhibition is a hypothesis motivated by benzodiazepine responses and reduced iomazenil binding in a small study of akinetic catatonia. Receptor-ligand binding is a proxy for receptor availability, not a direct measure of inhibitory synaptic transmission. Matching psychiatric controls for diagnosis and medication strengthens the comparison but does not eliminate residual confounding or establish causality.

nodes.description: A distributed-network model integrates structural and functional imaging associations across cortico-striatal-thalamic, cortico-cerebellar, orbitofrontal, cingulate and motor-premotor regions. Multimodal MRI in schizophrenia-spectrum participants identifies candidate circuits, but does not establish a shared causal substrate across every etiology or catatonic presentation. Most neurochemical-to-network links remain mechanistic hypotheses.

nodes.description: Lorazepam is a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors and a first-line treatment for catatonia. In an open prospective study, signs resolved in 16 of 21 patients completing a lorazepam trial; this is an uncontrolled response proportion. Treatment is titrated to clinical response and tolerability, with attention to sedation and respiratory effects. Benzodiazepines are tapered rather than stopped abruptly because withdrawal can precipitate recurrence. Response varies with clinical context and may be less reliable in chronic catatonia associated with schizophrenia. When catatonia follows benzodiazepine withdrawal, a benzodiazepine can be reinstated. Older adults may respond to lower doses.

nodes.description: A small emotional-task fMRI study of postacute akinetic catatonia found altered orbitofrontal activation and functional connectivity with premotor cortex. Behavioral and affective symptom scores correlated with orbitofrontal activity, while motor symptoms were related to medial prefrontal activity. A persistent trait abnormality is one interpretation, but postacute sampling cannot distinguish predisposition from consequences of illness or treatment.

nodes.description: Reduced striatal dopamine signaling is a proposed contributor to hypokinetic catatonia. Human imaging observations are sparse and measure presynaptic synthesis, storage or transporter availability rather than the complete signaling pathway. The direct/indirect basal-ganglia pathway model is mechanistic background; its full sequence has not been demonstrated in catatonia. Pharmacological reports and overlap with neuroleptic malignant syndrome support investigation but are not a universal explanation.
